I've been working this land since I was sixteen. My father showed me, and I watch what the good farmers in our village do. Nine mu is what I have, same as last year. Wheat in winter, corn in summer — everyone here does it this way.

For my wheat, I buy two bags of compound fertilizer before sowing — that's 100 jin per mu of the 15-15-15 stuff from the dealer in town. Then when the wheat stands up in spring, I spread urea, maybe 30 jin per mu. Any less and the leaves turn yellow — I saw that happen to my cousin two years ago, he tried to save money and lost half a sack per mu. Not worth it.

For corn, same idea — one bag compound at planting, then urea when it gets to my chest (what old people call the big trumpet stage). Corn eats more nitrogen than wheat, I can see it in how the leaves stay dark.

Seeds — I buy hybrid corn from the shop, everybody does, the old seeds give small ears. Wheat I buy improved variety, I pick what the dealer says the other people bought most.

Water — I have the well, so wheat gets watered three times: once before winter so it doesn't freeze, once in spring when it stands up, and once when the grain fills. Corn is summer, rain comes, but I still water once or twice if July is dry.

Spraying — once for weeds, once for aphids on wheat. Corn I spray for borer and weeds, two times.

For the ground — I rent the rotary tiller from the village service, costs me some yuan but beats hoeing. I don't plough deep every year, too expensive.

Yield — last year wheat gave me about 450 jin per mu, corn about 550. I expect the same, nothing big changed.
